title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an alleged insider misuse of law enforcement systems, not a failure of the systems themselves. A person with authorised access is accused of querying licence plate readers and a criminal justice database for personal reasons rather than police work. The failure sits at the point of legitimate access, where the same credentials that support policing also permit searches that have nothing to do with it.

Catching this kind of conduct requires auditing who queried what and why, and comparing those queries against case numbers or stated purposes. The reporting does not say whether any such audit existed, whether the searches were flagged automatically, or whether the woman was notified by the agency. It also does not establish how the conduct came to light.

The charges are allegations. An indictment is not a conviction, and the account of the woman who spoke out is her account. Nothing in the reporting establishes intent beyond what prosecutors have charged, and the outcome of the arraignment is not yet known.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff's deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, has been released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Prosecutors allege Rozar misused the sheriff's office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons between April 10 and May 1, 2024, including tracking a woman without her consent.

The woman, who asked to remain anonymous, said she hopes speaking out encourages other women to report abuse. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation led the multi-year investigation, which began after former Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested it in 2024, and Rozar was terminated when it started. He was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. His arraignment is scheduled for May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
